title: Cast handwheel
summary: sweep, pattern, root fillets, size table
description: A DIN 950 spoked handwheel in grey cast iron, 80 to 500 mm, with cranked oval spokes, a turned and polished rim, a keyed bore and a DIN 98 revolving handle on a boss at the standard's radius, painted machine green.
process: Sand casting, turning, keyway broaching, tapping

difficulty.rationale: Two standard tables drive it through dependent choice ranges; a swept oval along a tangent-solved crank, a pattern, chain fillets with careful edge names, a conditional feature, a lug and seat ordered around kernel cost, closed-form and draft proofs; planar paths, no freeform surfacing.

materials: Grey cast iron EN-GJL-200, machine-green enamel, rim turned and polished

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Passed with one gap: diameter 199.999 mm, depth 44.99996 mm, section area 715.87 mm² as the closed form, casting 1.990 kg and handle 0.241 kg as this example's; 9 of 10 checks pass, the spokes' upper-face draft not proven (F-102); root fillets named for three spokes only, so the five-spoke sizes kept two sharp spokes unnoticed (turn 3 now says so); about 130 steps.
